identity: SCRIPTURE - the complete Surat al-Furqan (Quran 25), all 77 ayat, in Uthmani orthography with diacritics and verse markers stripped (السموت، الملئكة، ءالهة، الأمثل، الشيطن، القرءان، بايتنا، حيوة). 893 tokens, ZERO <NL>.
law: THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (0k). 893 tokens / 77 ayat = 11.6 tokens per verse, min 4 (v.46 thumma qabadnahu ilayna qabdan yasira), max 22. Inside a verse NOTHING cuts.
reasoning: This sura rhymes almost entirely in -ira / -ura / -ila / -ama, and that rhyme IS the verse marker: nadhira, taqdira, nushura, wa-zura, wa-asila, rahima ... imama, wa-salama, wa-maqama, lizama. Reading the rhyme off the text is more reliable than any syntactic test and it is what I used. The rhyme also disambiguates the six verses that end in sabila (9, 27, 34, 42, 44, 57), the three in nushura (3, 40, 47), the three in kathira (14, 38, 49) and the three in kabira (19, 21, 52) - each is found in sequence, and the last one lands exactly on the final token, which is the alignment proof. Every PASS-2 trigger in the sura was suppressed: the imperatives qul (vv. 6, 15, 57, 77), unzur (9), fa-la tuti al-kafirin wa-jahidhum (52), wa-tawakkal ... wa-sabbih (58) - E6 is dead in scripture (0k); bal at vv. 11 and 44; the wa-huwa alladhi frames at 47, 48, 53, 54, 62, which are five SEPARATE verses and therefore five boundaries, not a merged isocolon; and the long wa-lladhina catalogue of the servants of the Merciful (vv. 63-76), where fourteen parallel relative clauses are fourteen separate verses - the one place where E1-style parallelism and the verse law agree. The hardest stretch was vv. 63-68, whose verses are 4-11 tokens and whose rhyme changes from -ama to -ama again (salama / qiyama / gharama / maqama / qawama / athama); I trusted the rhyme and the known verse count rather than length.
